title: Health priority queue and regional circuit-breaker matrix for staged readiness and autoscaler stability
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Introduce a lightweight health-priority queue and a regional circuit-breaker matrix to stabilize autoscaling behavior during partial degradations. Goal: reduce cascading autoscale churn while preserving critical SLOs (p95 latency and availability) during multi-region incidents. Replace brittle one-size-fits-all readiness timeouts with staged readiness that surfaces service health in priority tiers, combined with a token-based backpressure mechanism for ingress and a region-to-region circuit-breaker policy for failover decisions.
steps: Design health-priority queue data model and per-instance health weights
Prototype token-based ingress backpressure client and server shim
Implement staged readiness states (healthy, degraded-priority, degraded-low, draining)
Add regional circuit-breaker matrix with policy authoring and runtime evaluation
Integrate with autoscaler to honor priority tiers and apply derating/hysteresis
End-to-end integration tests with synthetic transaction harness
Canary rollout in us-west-2 with telemetry and rollback hooks
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler path reduces 95th percentile scaling oscillations by >=30% in synthetic partial-failure tests
Critical SLO (p95 latency) remains within target for high-priority traffic during single-region degradation
Regional circuit-breaker opens and routes failover traffic according to matrix rules within 15s of threshold breach
No increase in error rate for healthy-region requests after canary rollout
Documentation for ops runbook and policy authoring published

notes: Trade-offs: prioritizing critical traffic protects SLOs but can starve background work; mitigation is a soft-replenish for low-priority tokens during steady state.
Risk: incorrect weight function could cause underutilization — initial canary will cap derating to 30% until observed metrics are stable.
Fallback: if regional circuit decision oscillates, we add a minimum open-window and require consecutive breaches before flip.
Compatibility: designed to work with both Dedicated and Hosted modes; private deployments may tune token counts via config
